source_title: Algebraic Approaches for the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem over Prime Fields

review_provenance.method: Independent review packet followed by direct primary-source confirmation.
review_provenance.boundary: The record binds claim locations and paraphrases. The paper leaves asymptotic complexity open and its experiments do not establish an advantage over generic algorithms.

claims.paraphrase: After sampling a and b and forming the target point (X,Y)=aP+bQ, Algorithm 1 solves one Semaev equation S_(m+1)(x_11,...,x_m1,X)=0 together with m copies of the composed-map chain x_(i,j+1)=L_j(x_(i,j)) and the terminal equations L_(n')(x_(i,n'))=0. Rational-map denominators are moved to the left-hand sides.
claims.boundary: The printed Step 4c checks whether recovered factor-base points satisfy sum_i P_i=0 and does not explicitly bind that check to the sampled target (X,Y), even though X occurs in System (4). A target-bound signed elliptic-curve recovery check is therefore a repository completion justified by summation-polynomial semantics, not a verbatim source claim.

claims.paraphrase: If p-1=r times the product of factors p_i and their product is about p^(1/m), the source takes the multiplicative subgroup of that product order, sets L_j(x)=x^(p_j) for j<n', sets L_(n')(x)=1-x^(p_(n')), and composes the maps. A coset variant is also mentioned.
claims.boundary: This specifies the root-map construction, not a fast solver for System (4). Calling every specialized component low degree requires an explicit arithmetic-circuit cost; for secp256k1 the selected factorization contains the degree-13441 terminal component.

claims.paraphrase: In a unit-cost model the source defines preprocessing P(p,m) and System-(4) solving time T(E,m,L), estimates decompositions by (deg L)^m/(m!p), and writes total cost P(p,m)+(m!p/(deg L)^(m-1))T(E,m,L)+(deg L)^omega. At the balance (deg L)^m approximately m!p, beating square-root work requires T below p^(1/2-1/m).
claims.boundary: The paper explicitly leaves the complexity open and reports that it had not investigated an algorithm better than Groebner-basis methods for System (4). The formula is a partial model: it does not prove relation independence, recovery completeness, a common-unit comparison, or an end-to-end secp256k1 advantage.

claims.paraphrase: The first construction requires a B-smooth divisor of p-1 with size approximately p^(1/m), uses its multiplicative subgroup or a coset as the root set of a composed map, and inserts those constraints into the Semaev relation system.
claims.boundary: Raw factor-base size is only an applicability condition. Solver, recovery, relation collection, linear algebra, and preprocessing remain part of the total cost.

claims.paraphrase: For an arbitrary base-field prime, the second construction searches for an auxiliary curve over the same field whose order contains a B-smooth factor of size approximately p^(1/m). A self-isogeny of that auxiliary curve defines the composed root map used for the original target curve's factor-base coordinates.
claims.boundary: The auxiliary curve is not required to be related to the target curve beyond sharing the field. Its search cost, map construction, generalized-root solving, recovery, and total attack cost must all be priced.

claims.paraphrase: The paper estimates the expected number of decompositions per target as (deg L)^m divided by m! times p, charges relation collection by the reciprocal yield, and identifies (deg L)^m approximately m! times p as the balance point for its partial cost analysis.
claims.boundary: This is a heuristic expectation in the paper's unit-cost model. It does not bound T(E,m,L), prove independent relations, price recovery or preprocessing fully, or establish an advantage over Pollard rho.
